key_insight: SuperCond-GNN learns superconducting circuit voltage distributions from graph-structured equivalent circuits, enabling fast surrogate prediction across varying HTS tape-stack topologies and operating conditions.
engineering_relevance: It offers a scalable alternative to repeated circuit solves for design exploration, current-sharing analysis, and real-time monitoring of HTS magnets.
method: Map HTS magnet tape stacks to lumped-element circuit graphs
Train a message-passing GNN to predict nodal voltages from topology, material properties, and current
Optionally add Kirchhoff’s current-law regularization and test zero-shot/few-shot generalization
evidence_signal: Across tape-stack circuits up to 10 tapes, the surrogate achieves a mean MAPE of 4.3% within the prescribed design space.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on a limited tape-stack regime, so transfer to larger or more complex HTS magnet geometries may require additional validation and retraining.
paper_title: SuperCond-GNN: Scalable Graph Neural Network Surrogate for Superconducting Circuit Simulations
